title: Customer Account Management
include_extend_relationships: Login as Customer <<include>> Get User Details
Register Account <<include>> Check Email Already Registered
Register Account <<extend>> Receive Registration Confirmation Email

key_classes.name: RegisterSrv
key_classes.logic: Reads form params (username, mobile, email, address, pincode, password, confirmPassword), validates password match, creates UserBean, calls UserServiceImpl.registerUser(user), forwards to register.jsp

key_classes.name: LoginSrv
key_classes.logic: Reads username, password, usertype. If admin: hardcoded check (admin@gmail.com/admin) → session → adminViewProduct.jsp. If customer: calls isValidCredential() → if valid calls getUserDetails() → sets session (userdata, username, password, usertype) → userHome.jsp; else login.jsp with error

key_classes.name: LogoutSrv
key_classes.logic: Nullifies session attributes (username, password, usertype, userdata), forwards to login.jsp with success message

key_classes.name: UserService
methods: registerUser(String userName, Long mobileNo, String emailId, String address, int pinCode, String password): String

key_classes.name: UserServiceImpl
key_classes.logic: registerUser checks isRegistered first (prevents duplicates), inserts into DB via PreparedStatement, sends confirmation email via MailMessage.registrationSuccess(). isValidCredential queries DB for email+password match. getUserDetails fetches full UserBean from DB.

important_notes: Admin login uses hardcoded credentials (admin@gmail.com / admin) — no DB call. Customer login uses DB via UserServiceImpl. Registration sends a confirmation email. LogoutSrv has no service layer dependency — operates on HttpSession directly. UserServiceImpl directly uses JDBC (no ORM).
